entities.summary: Appius Annius Trebonius Gallus was a Roman senator and member of the aristocracy during the reign of Emperor Trajan. Born into a prominent equestrian family, he rose through the ranks to become ordinary consul in 108 AD, alongside Marcus Atilius Bradua. Trebonius Gallus's tenure as consul was marked by his involvement in the Roman administration of the province of Dacia, which would later become a significant factor in the empire's expansion. His legacy is largely forgotten in modern times, but his contributions to the Roman state's governance and administrative practices remain an important aspect of understanding the empire's growth and development. As the Roman Empire continued to expand its borders, Trebonius Gallus's work on the administrative structures of Dacia served as a model for future emperors, demonstrating the importance of effective governance in maintaining the empire's power and stability.
